chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever enters Mecca for Hajj on behalf of another, then stays for a year, he is considered a resident of Mecca (Makki). So when he intends to perform Hajj for himself, or intends to perform Umrah after having left from Arafat, it is not for him to enter the state of Ihram in Mecca, but he must go out to the Miqat (juncture), and every time he turns back, he must return to the Miqat.

key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: To enter the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Where should a resident of Mecca enter the state of Ihram for Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the status of a 'Makki' (resident of Mecca) who has stayed for a year after performing Hajj on behalf of another, establishing that they must exit to a Miqat to perform their own Hajj or Umrah, as they cannot assume Ihram within the city limits. This ruling highlights the distinct legal category of Mecca's residents compared to pilgrims from outside, ensuring the sanctity of the city's boundaries during the ritual state. The requirement to return to the Miqat if one leaves underscores the strict geographical parameters of Ihram for locals.
